subject.title: fix(openrouter): apply request policy to music generation requests

question: Should OpenRouter music generation honor the existing provider-level allowPrivateNetwork opt-in even though the OpenRouter video capability currently retains an explicit private-network denial?
rationale: The implementation follows the documented shared request-policy contract, but the sibling difference leaves capability scope as an intentional security-boundary choice rather than a purely mechanical review decision.

options.title: Honor explicit opt-in
options.body: Allow music generation to use the existing operator-controlled private-network option while keeping the restrictive default and focused coverage.

options.title: Preserve music denial
options.body: Forward headers, proxy, TLS, and other request policy while retaining allowPrivateNetwork:false for this capability.

options.title: Unify media policy first
options.body: Pause this PR until music and video use one explicitly documented OpenRouter media security policy.

recommendation.title: Honor explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Allow music generation to use the existing operator-controlled private-network option while keeping the restrictive default and focused coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared provider transport and network-policy history makes this the strongest available owner for the capability-scope decision.
